HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NARENDRA SINGH DHADDHA
Judgment Date of Judgment 10/05/2024 1.

The present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the claimants-appellants (for short 'the claimants') dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 22.07.2021 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Judge, Communal Riots Cases),
Jaipur Metropolitan, Jaipur (for short 'the Tribunal') in Claim Case No.416/2017, whereby the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.13,74,800/- along (2 of 4) [CMA-1877/2021] with interest @ 6%
per annum from the date of filing the claim petition as compensation in favour of the claimants.

Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Judge, Communal Riots Cases),
Jaipur Metropolitan, Jaipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The Tribunal on the basis of the pleading of the parties, framed the issues and evaluated the evidence on record.

After hearing counsel for the parties, decided the claim petition of the claimants Smt. Vijay Laxmi Pareek W/O Shri Rakesh ... vs Surendra Singh Son Of Shri Jabbar Singh ... on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17451575/
1 and awarded the amount as indicated above.

entities.text: Rakesh ... vs Surendra Singh Son Of Shri Jabbar Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that the Tribunal has wrongly considered the income of the deceased as Rs.7,900/- per month.

Learned counsel for the claimants further submits that the deceased was working in Mahavir Viklang Samiti, Malviya Nagar, Jaipur and his income was Rs.15,000/- per month after doing overtime in two shifts.
So, income of the deceased be considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Learned counsel for the claimants further submits that the Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards loss of estate, whereas it should be Rs.15,000/-.
So, judgment and award of the Tribunal may be modified.

4. Learned counsel for the insurance company has opposed the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the claimants and submitted that the finding of the Tribunal does not suffer from any infirmity or illegality.
So, appeal be dismissed.

5. I have considered the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the claimants as well as learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company and perused the judgment dated 22.07.2021.
6.
It is an admitted position that the claimants failed to adduce any cogent evidence that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

As per Salary Certificate (Exhibit-16) of the deceased,
his income was Rs.8,000/- per month.

So, in my considered (3 of 4) [CMA-1877/2021] opinion,
Tribunal has not committed any error in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs. 7,900/- per month after deducting the tax amount of Rs.100/- but the Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards loss of estate, whereas it should be Rs. 15,000/-.

So, the judgment of the Tribunal is modified to the extent as under:-
A n n u a l I n c o m e 7 , 9 0 0 X 1 2 = R s . 9 4 , 8 0 0 / - A d d 5 0 % t o w a r d s f u t u r e 94,800+47,400=1,42,200/- prospects, as awarded by the Tribunal 1/2 is to be deducted for 1,42,200-71,100=Rs.71,100/- personal expenses of the deceased According to the age of the 71,100 X18=Rs.12,79,800/- deceased i.e. 20 years and one month, Multiplier 18 to be applied Loss of Love and Affection to Rs.80,000/-
 the claimants,as awarded by  the Tribunal (40,000X 2)
 Loss of Estate(+) Rs.15,000/-
 Funeral Expenses(+), as Rs.15,000/-
 awarded by the Tribunal  Total  Rs.13,89,800/-
 Less amount awarded by the  Tribunal Rs.13,74,800/-
 Enhanced Amount of  compensation 13,89,800-13,74,800  =Rs.15,000/-
Smt. Vijay Laxmi Pareek W/O Shri Rakesh ... vs Surendra Singh Son Of Shri Jabbar Singh ... on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17451575/
2 7.

In view of the above, the claimants are entitled to get a further sum of Rs.15,000/-
as compensation.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit enhanced amount of Rs.
Rs.15,000/- (13,89,800-13,74,800) with the Tribunal within a period of two months from the date of receipt of certified copy of (4 of 4) [CMA-1877/2021] this order.
On deposition of the said amount, the claimants shall be entitled to withdrawn the same.

The enhanced amount shall carry @
6% interest per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the actual payment is made.
8. Rest part of the impugned judgment shall remain unchanged.
Impugned judgment and award is modified accordingly.
9. Consequently, the appeal is partly allowed.
10. Pending application(s), if any, also stand(s) disposed of.

(NARENDRA SINGH DHADDHA),J Gourav/375 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
